  "title": "LACVLA: Enforcing Language-Affordance Grounding via Consistency Objectives for Zero-Shot Cross-Category VLA Manipulation",
  "core_problem": "How can end-to-end VLA models achieve zero-shot manipulation transfer to entirely unseen object categories — objects with no visual precedent in training — given that (1) cross-category transfer fundamentally requires spatial grounding from language (the only cue that specifies WHERE to interact on a novel object), yet (2) current VLAs largely ignore language instructions (LIBERO-Plus, CVPR 2026; LangGap, Mar 2026), a failure mode that is survivable in-distribution but catastrophic when visual priors are absent?",
  "opportunity": "Cross-category zero-shot manipulation — generalizing to objects never seen during training — remains an open challenge: even strong VLAs like π₀.₅ and GR00T-N1.6 fail on affordance generalization across object variants (BusyBox, Feb 2026), and A0 (ICCV 2025) achieves cross-category transfer via 1M contact points but without language conditioning. The fundamental bottleneck is that novel objects lack visual priors, so language must serve as the primary guide for spatial grounding — yet diagnostic work shows VLAs systematically ignore language. LIBERO-Plus (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2510.13626) reveals VLAs exhibit positional bias rather than semantic understanding; LangGap (arXiv 2603.00592, Mar 2026) quantifies this: VLAs with 95%+ standard success largely ignore language, and targeted data augmentation hits a ceiling (0%→28% multi-task). LIBERO-Para (Mar 2026) shows 22–52pp drops under paraphrased instructions, with 80–96% of failures from planning-level trajectory divergence. Shin (Mar 2026) achieves only +1.71pp via LLM-generated paraphrase augmentation, consistent with LangGap's ceiling finding. Recent approaches address aspects of this problem but not the full combination: spatial grounding methods (ST4VLA, ICLR 2026; SpatialVLA, RSS 2025) improve performance broadly but do not structurally guarantee language conditioning — a model can learn spatial shortcuts within training categories. GuidedVLA (RSS 2026) supervises individual attention heads with auxiliary signals but uses 3 predefined factor types without cross-category transfer focus. ProGAL-VLA (Apr 2026) imposes a verified grounding bottleneck via 3D entity-centric graphs and symbolic sub-goals, improving robustness (30.3%→71.5% on LIBERO-Plus perturbations) but requires explicit entity recognition rather than open-vocabulary affordance transfer. PPCL (EACL 2024) showed consistency regularization beats augmentation with 10× fewer samples in NLP. The opportunity: an affordance-gated architectural bottleneck with self-supervised consistency objectives that structurally forces language to condition spatial grounding — making language a mandatory pathway for action generation — enabling genuine cross-category zero-shot transfer without 3D sensors, expensive cross-category annotations, or modular decomposition.",
  "landscape": "The VLA-affordance landscape has six relevant lineages, none of which combines architectural enforcement of language conditioning, self-supervised consistency on spatial affordance representations, and cross-category zero-shot transfer as the primary target. (1) Spatially-guided VLAs: ST4VLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2602.10109) introduces dual-system spatial grounding (Qwen2.5-VL planner + DiT/DINOv2 action expert), achieving 95.9% LIBERO average (98.0% Spatial, 99.0% Object, 93.8% Goal, 92.6% Long), 72%/61% attribute/spatial paraphrase robustness (vs π₀: 32%/31%), and 62% on new object instances (vs π₀: 32%, GR00T N1: 46%). This is LACVLA's strongest baseline — the null hypothesis is 'does explicit affordance consistency add value beyond spatial grounding alone?' InternVLA-M1 (arXiv 2510.13778) extends this with affordance recognition and chain-of-thought reasoning. SpatialVLA (RSS 2025, arXiv 2501.15830) introduces Ego3D Position Encoding and Adaptive Action Grids. Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.12276) aligns VLM features with 3D foundation models without 3D input at inference. All improve spatial understanding but none guarantees language conditions the spatial representation. (2) Supervised intermediate representation guidance: GuidedVLA (RSS 2026, arXiv 2605.12369) treats the action decoder as an assembly of functional components, supervising individual attention heads with auxiliary signals for three predefined factor types: object grounding (attention mass loss over detected object masks), spatial geometry (depth encoder feature constraint), and temporal skill logic (KL-divergence skill classification). Built on π₀, achieves 75.4% on LIBERO-Plus (vs 68.2% baseline), 90.63% on RoboTwin 2.0. Architectural parallel to LACVLA: both use explicit supervision on intermediate representations to improve VLA grounding. Key differences: GuidedVLA uses 3 predefined factor types (not open-vocabulary), does not use consistency objectives on heatmaps, does not produce affordance heatmaps, and does not target cross-category zero-shot transfer. LACVLA's affordance readout with stop-gradient bottleneck produces open-vocabulary spatial heatmaps enforced via self-supervised consistency — a fundamentally different supervision signal (consistency between paraphrases vs. factor-specific auxiliary losses). (3) Language grounding diagnostics and solutions: LIBERO-Plus (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2510.13626) reveals VLAs are insensitive to language and exhibit positional bias. LangGap (arXiv 2603.00592, Mar 2026) confirms VLAs ignore language and shows augmentation's ceiling (28% multi-task). LIBERO-Para (arXiv 2603.28301, Mar 2026) quantifies paraphrase fragility (22–52pp drops). Shin (arXiv 2603.16044, Mar 2026) achieves only +1.71pp via augmentation. ProGAL-VLA (arXiv 2604.09824, Apr 2026) constructs a 3D entity-centric graph with symbolic sub-goals and Grounding Alignment Contrastive loss, imposing a verified grounding bottleneck — achieves 71.5% robustness on LIBERO-Plus (up from 30.3%), but requires explicit entity recognition and 3D scene graphs, not applicable to open-vocabulary affordance transfer across unseen categories. Stable Language Guidance (ACL 2026, arXiv 2601.04052) addresses modality collapse at inference via residual steering — complementary to LACVLA's training-time approach. Attention recalibration (arXiv 2603.06001) provides train-free inference-time fix for attention sink dynamics but does not change learned representations. (4) Modular affordance-then-action pipelines: RT-Affordance (arXiv 2411.02704), UAD (ICRA 2025), RAM (CoRL 2024), RAAP (arXiv 2603.29419, Mar 2026), AffordDP (CVPR 2025), RoboMAP (arXiv 2510.10912), A0 (ICCV 2025, arXiv 2504.12636), and GLOVER++ (CoRL 2025, arXiv 2505.11865) all produce affordance representations but feed them to separate downstream planners/policies, sacrificing end-to-end optimization. A0 achieves zero-shot cross-category transfer via 1M contact points but without language conditioning. (5) Architectural bottleneck enforcement: DIAL (arXiv 2603.29844, Mar 2026) enforces a latent intent bottleneck via inverse dynamics — the action head MUST use predicted latent intent. This inspires LACVLA's affordance-gated bottleneck (stop-gradient on VLM features, affordance map as spatial attention gate). (6) Cross-category zero-shot benchmarks: AGNOSTOS/X-ICM (arXiv 2505.15660) provides 23 unseen manipulation tasks. VLA² (arXiv 2510.14902) uses agentic retrieval for unseen concepts. BusyBox (arXiv 2602.05441, Feb 2026) is a physical benchmark where 6 reconfigurable modules test affordance generalization — even π₀.₅ and GR00T-N1.6 fail on shuffled configurations despite identical affordances, demonstrating that affordance generalization remains unsolved. Gap: No existing work combines (a) architectural enforcement that language must condition spatial features via stop-gradient bottleneck, (b) self-supervised consistency objectives on affordance heatmaps (not raw actions, not predefined factor types), and (c) cross-category zero-shot transfer as the primary evaluation target.",
  "approach": "We propose LACVLA, an end-to-end VLA that structurally forces language to condition spatial affordance grounding through an affordance-gated bottleneck and self-supervised consistency objectives, enabling zero-shot cross-category manipulation transfer.

Architecture — Affordance-Gated Bottleneck (inspired by DIAL's latent intent bottleneck): Built on a 4B–7B VLM backbone (Qwen2-VL-4B via StarVLA or PaliGemma2) with LoRA fine-tuning. The architecture has three components:
(a) Affordance Readout: A cross-attention layer where language instruction tokens attend over intermediate VLM visual features (layer ~16 of 32 for Qwen2-VL), producing a dense affordance heatmap over the image. This encodes WHERE to interact, conditioned on the instruction. Architecture: single cross-attention + LayerNorm + linear projection to H×W heatmap, <5M parameters.
(b) Stop-Gradient Bottleneck: VLM intermediate visual features are passed through a stop-gradient before reaching the action head. The action head receives: affordance_heatmap ⊙ sg(VLM_visual_features) + proprioceptive_state. The affordance map acts as a spatial attention gate — if the model produces a uniform (language-ignoring) affordance map, the action head receives unselective visual features with no spatial focus, degrading performance. Unlike GuidedVLA's factor-specific head supervision (predefined types, direct auxiliary losses), LACVLA's stop-gradient ensures no task-semantic gradient flows through the non-affordance pathway — the action head CANNOT learn to extract task information from raw VLM features, and the affordance readout is open-vocabulary rather than restricted to predefined factor categories.
(c) Flow-Matching Action Head: A lightweight DiT (Diffusion Transformer) that generates trajectory chunks conditioned on the affordance-gated visual features + proprioceptive state, following the flow-matching formulation.

Training Objectives — Three jointly optimized losses with phased schedule:
(1) Instruction-Paraphrase Affordance Consistency (IPAC): Given the same visual scene and K LLM-generated paraphrases of the same task instruction (e.g., 'grab the mug handle' vs. 'grasp the cup by its handle'), the affordance maps must be consistent (KL divergence penalty on spatial heatmaps). This transfers the consistency regularization principle from PPCL (EACL 2024) — which showed consistency > augmentation with 10× less data in NLP — to spatial affordance heatmaps. Unlike Shin (2026), who uses paraphrases purely as data augmentation (+1.71pp), IPAC uses them as a regularization signal constraining affordance geometry. Paraphrases generated offline by LLM — free, unlimited supervision.
(2) Instruction-Discriminative Affordance (IDA): Given the same visual scene and two semantically different instructions (e.g., 'pick up the mug by its handle' vs. 'pour from the mug'), the affordance maps must diverge (margin-based divergence loss). This prevents degenerate consistency collapse where the model produces instruction-invariant heatmaps to trivially satisfy IPAC. Different-instruction pairs come naturally from multi-task robot datasets.
(3) Action-Grounded Affordance (AGA): Standard flow-matching loss for trajectory prediction through the affordance-gated bottleneck. This grounds the affordance map in manipulation-relevant contact regions via end-to-end backpropagation through the gating mechanism.

Phased Training Schedule:
Phase 1 — Affordance Readout Pre-training: PRIMARY path: pre-train on HOVA-500K with cross-attention readout predicting contact-point Gaussian heatmaps (σ proportional to object scale) conditioned on action-label text prompts from 675 action categories. Viewpoint augmentation (random crop, perspective warp, ego→third-person style augmentation) addresses the ego-centric domain gap. FALLBACK path (if domain gap diagnostic fails): self-supervised affordance readout initialization using robot data alone — extract pseudo-affordance Gaussian heatmaps from gripper position at grasp/contact time in robot trajectory data (well-established technique: text-driven affordance learning with pseudo-labels, trajectory-based contact recovery). This produces lower-coverage but higher-fidelity affordance supervision for the robot observation domain. Diagnostic checkpoint: evaluate pre-trained affordance readout on a held-out set of robot observation images; if domain gap degrades affordance quality below threshold (mean IoU < 0.3 between predicted heatmap peak and gripper contact region), switch to fallback path. Ablation of HOVA-500K vs. self-supervised initialization determines whether HOVA-500K is necessary, de-risking the paper from the HOVA-500K dependency.
Phase 2 — End-to-end VLA training (steps 0–N): Fine-tune full model (VLM via LoRA + pre-trained affordance readout + flow-matching action head) on robot data. Sub-phases: (2a) AGA only for 10% of training — establish action grounding baseline. (2b) Add IPAC at 10% — enforce consistency while action loss stabilizes gradients. (2c) Ramp IDA from 0 to full weight over 15% of training via linear warmup, monitored by: (i) affordance entropy H(A) — if H(A) < 0.3 × H_max, increase IDA weight by 50%; (ii) instruction-discriminability D = mean pairwise KL between different-instruction maps on validation set — if D < 0.5, halt IPAC and boost IDA. GradNorm-style gradient normalization across the three losses balances training rates automatically.

Why Affordance Maps (Not Raw Actions) for Consistency: Affordance maps capture WHERE to interact — the geometric invariant across paraphrases and across categories sharing functional parts. Action distributions conflate WHERE + HOW + WHEN (trajectory shape, timing, force), making consistency regularization noisier. For cross-category transfer, WHERE is what transfers (handle locations generalize across mugs/cups/pitchers), while HOW adapts to object-specific geometry. This argument is validated empirically by ablation #5.

Cross-Object Functional Consistency via HOVA-500K: Group HOVA-500K images by shared action labels (675 categories) and apply soft KL penalty between affordance maps of same-action images from different object categories. This provides weak supervision for cross-category affordance consistency without requiring part-level functional equivalence annotations.

Data Pipeline: Open X-Embodiment and DROID for robot trajectories, HOVA-500K for affordance pre-training and cross-object grouping (with self-supervised robot-data fallback), LLM-generated instruction paraphrases (Qwen3 or GPT-4) for IPAC pairs.

Ablation Design (6 variants, streamlined to fit compute budget while retaining all core tests):
(1) Full LACVLA — affordance-gated bottleneck + IPAC + IDA + AGA
(2) Bottleneck analysis (merged): (a) No affordance bottleneck — direct VLA without affordance readout; (b) Bottleneck + AGA only, no consistency losses — tests whether architectural bottleneck alone suffices. Both sub-conditions use identical training data and hyperparameters; affordance map quality (entropy, instruction-discriminability) tracked for sub-condition (b) to diagnose whether the bottleneck induces meaningful affordance structure without consistency enforcement.
(3) Modular composition — frozen GLOVER++ affordance → separate policy (tests end-to-end vs. modular)
(4) Shin-style augmentation — paraphrases added as training data, no consistency loss (tests data augmentation ceiling, paralleling PPCL's NLP finding)
(5) IPAC on raw actions — KL divergence between action distributions under paraphrased instructions, no affordance readout (CRITICAL: tests whether isolating WHERE via affordance maps outperforms consistency on conflated action distributions — if affordance maps win, that's the paper's key finding; if raw actions work comparably, the affordance readout is unnecessary overhead)
(6) ST4VLA-style spatial grounding + IPAC on features — spatial grounding pre-training + consistency on intermediate VLM features without affordance readout (tests whether explicit affordance structure adds value beyond strong spatial pre-training + consistency)

Evaluation Protocol — Primary (Cross-Category Zero-Shot Transfer):
(a) Held-out object category experiments: partition LIBERO/DROID object categories into train/test sets, test on entirely unseen categories with both standard and paraphrased instructions
(b) HOVA-500K cross-category transfer tests: train on K action categories with one set of objects (e.g., 'pour from pitcher'), test on same actions with different object categories (e.g., 'pour from kettle') — constructed from HOVA-500K's 675 shared action labels
(c) AGNOSTOS benchmark (arXiv 2505.15660) for cross-task zero-shot evaluation (23 unseen tasks)
(d) BusyBox (arXiv 2602.05441) supplementary evaluation: if physical hardware is available, test LACVLA on shuffled BusyBox configurations where even π₀.₅ and GR00T-N1.6 fail — directly measures affordance generalization across visual variants with identical functional affordances
(e) Real-world evaluation on 5+ unseen object categories across at least 3 manipulation primitives (grasp, pour, push)

Evaluation Protocol — Secondary:
(f) LIBERO-Para benchmark with PRIDE metric for paraphrase robustness (direct comparison with ST4VLA's 72%/61%)
(g) LangGap protocol for language grounding quality (targeting improvement over the 28% multi-task ceiling)
(h) Affogato for affordance quality assessment
(i) Standard LIBERO (Spatial, Object, Goal, Long) for in-distribution comparison with ST4VLA (95.9% avg)

  "description": "We address cross-category zero-shot manipulation transfer — generalizing to objects with no visual precedent in training — where language is the only available guide for spatial grounding on novel objects. We show that the well-documented language-ignoring failure in VLAs (LIBERO-Plus, CVPR 2026; LangGap, Mar 2026) is particularly catastrophic in this setting: visual priors and layout memorization cannot compensate when the object itself is unseen. Existing approaches either improve spatial understanding without guaranteeing language conditions the representation (ST4VLA, SpatialVLA, Spatial Forcing), supervise predefined intermediate factor types without cross-category affordance transfer (GuidedVLA, RSS 2026), impose grounding bottlenecks requiring explicit entity recognition (ProGAL-VLA), or produce affordance representations in modular pipelines sacrificing end-to-end optimization (A0, GLOVER++, RT-Affordance). LACVLA proposes an affordance-gated architectural bottleneck, inspired by DIAL's latent intent bottleneck, that structurally forces all task-relevant spatial information through a language-conditioned affordance map: VLM intermediate features pass through stop-gradient before the action head, which receives affordance_heatmap ⊙ sg(visual_features) + proprioceptive_state. The affordance map (produced via cross-attention between VLM features and language tokens) acts as a spatial attention gate — a uniform (language-ignoring) map yields unselective features and degraded performance. Self-supervised consistency objectives enforce language-affordance grounding: IPAC ensures semantically equivalent instructions produce identical affordance maps (transferring PPCL's consistency > augmentation principle from NLP to spatial heatmaps), while IDA ensures semantically different instructions produce divergent maps (preventing collapse). # Paper Analysis: RobustVLA

## Full Abstract
The paper evaluates Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models' resilience across 17 perturbations spanning four modalities. Key findings: actions represent the most vulnerable modality; existing visual-robustness methods don't transfer to other modalities; pi0 shows superior robustness. The authors propose RobustVLA, which applies offline robust optimization against worst-case action noise and enforces consistent actions across input variations preserving task semantics.

## Key Method Details

**Output Robustness:** The approach performs "offline robust optimization against worst-case action noise that maximizes mismatch in flow matching objective," functioning as adversarial training combined with label smoothing and outlier penalization.

**Input Robustness & Consistency Mechanism:** The method "enforce[s] consistent actions across input variations that preserve task semantics." This consistency approach ensures stable predictions when encountering perturbed inputs while maintaining semantic task understanding.

**Multi-perturbation Handling:** Authors formulate robustness as a multi-armed bandit problem, applying upper confidence bound algorithms to automatically identify the most harmful noise types.

## Main Results

On LIBERO benchmarks:
- 12.6% absolute gains (pi0 backbone)
- 10.4% gains (OpenVLA backbone)
- 50.6x faster inference than visual-robust BYOVLA

**Real-world FR5 robot performance:** With 25 demonstrations, RobustVLA outperforms pi0 by 65.6% success rate under multimodal perturbations; maintains 30% advantage even with abundant data.

## Benchmarks
- LIBERO (17 perturbations across 4 modalities)
- FR5 robot (real-world validation with 4 multimodal perturbations)

## Cross-Category Transfer
No explicit cross-category transfer is discussed in the provided content.

## (1) Input Consistency Mechanism

The consistency mechanism enforces invariant actions across perturbed inputs through adversarial training. Rather than using paraphrased instructions explicitly, the authors apply various perturbation types during training and optimize the flow-matching objective to produce similar actions.

The loss function is: "min_θ L^τ_π0 + λ_in max_ωi E[||v_θ(A^τ_t, ωi(o_t)) - u(A^τ_t|A_t)||²]"

This maximizes mismatch between clean and perturbed observations, forcing the model to maintain consistent outputs despite input variations.

The method operates at **action-level consistency only**. They directly regularize the flow-matching velocity field to produce matching action distributions under perturbed versus clean observations, without intermediate representation constraints.

Three instruction uncertainty types are tested:
- **Lexical transformations**: Word-level modifications
- **Syntactic transformations**: Sentence-level structural changes  
- **Adversarial prompts**: Instructions containing "ambiguity and distraction"

(a) Affordance Readout: A cross-attention layer where language instruction tokens attend over intermediate VLM visual features (layer ~16 of 32 for Qwen2-VL), producing a dense affordance heatmap over the image. This encodes WHERE to interact, conditioned on the instruction. Architecture: single cross-attention + LayerNorm + linear projection to H×W heatmap, <5M parameters.
(b) Stop-Gradient Bottleneck: VLM intermediate visual features are passed through a stop-gradient before reaching the action head. The action head receives: affordance_heatmap ⊙ sg(VLM_visual_features) + proprioceptive_state. The affordance map acts as a spatial attention gate — if the model produces a uniform (language-ignoring) affordance map, the action head receives unselective visual features with no spatial focus, degrading performance. Unlike AFI's inference-time 3D SAF plugin, LACVLA enforces affordance grounding architecturally during training without requiring 3D input.
(c) Flow-Matching Action Head: A lightweight DiT (Diffusion Transformer) that generates trajectory chunks conditioned on the affordance-gated visual features + proprioceptive state, following the flow-matching formulation.

RobustVLA enforces that paraphrased instructions produce the same actions; IPAC enforces that they produce the same spatial WHERE-to-interact maps, allowing the action head to independently adapt HOW-to-move. (2) Instruction-Discriminative Affordance (IDA): Given the same visual scene and two semantically different instructions (e.g., 'pick up the mug by its handle' vs. 'pour from the mug'), the affordance maps must diverge (margin-based divergence loss). This prevents degenerate consistency collapse where the model produces instruction-invariant heatmaps to trivially satisfy IPAC. (3) Action-Grounded Affordance (AGA): Standard flow-matching loss for trajectory prediction through the affordance-gated bottleneck. This grounds the affordance map in manipulation-relevant contact regions via end-to-end backpropagation through the gating mechanism.

Diagnostic checkpoint: evaluate pre-trained affordance readout on a held-out set of robot observation images; if domain gap degrades affordance quality below threshold (mean IoU < 0.3 between predicted heatmap peak and gripper contact region), switch to fallback path. Ablation of HOVA-500K vs. self-supervised initialization determines whether HOVA-500K is necessary.
Phase 2 — End-to-end VLA training (steps 0–N): Fine-tune full model (VLM via LoRA + pre-trained affordance readout + flow-matching action head) on robot data. Sub-phases: (2a) AGA only for 10% of training — establish action grounding baseline. (2b) Add IPAC at 10% — enforce consistency while action loss stabilizes gradients. (2c) Ramp IDA from 0 to full weight over 15% of training via linear warmup, monitored by: (i) affordance entropy H(A) — if H(A) < 0.3 × H_max, increase IDA weight by 50%; (ii) instruction-discriminability D = mean pairwise KL between different-instruction maps on validation set — if D < 0.5, halt IPAC and boost IDA. GradNorm-style gradient normalization across the three losses balances training rates automatically.

Why Affordance Maps (Not Raw Actions) for Consistency — The Central Hypothesis: Affordance maps capture WHERE to interact — the geometric invariant across paraphrases and across categories sharing functional parts. Action distributions conflate WHERE + HOW + WHEN (trajectory shape, timing, force), making consistency regularization noisier. RobustVLA (ICLR 2026) demonstrates that action-level consistency yields strong in-distribution robustness (+12.6% on π₀ across 17 perturbations). LACVLA hypothesizes that for cross-category transfer, isolating the spatial component is critical: WHERE is what transfers (handle locations generalize across mugs/cups/pitchers), while HOW adapts to object-specific geometry. Action-level consistency forces the entire trajectory to be invariant under paraphrases, which is correct within a category but may prevent the action head from adapting HOW-to-move when the same affordance (e.g., 'grasp the handle') appears on a geometrically different object. This hypothesis is directly tested by ablation #5.

(2) Bottleneck analysis (merged): (a) No affordance bottleneck — direct VLA without affordance readout; (b) Bottleneck + AGA only, no consistency losses — tests whether architectural bottleneck alone suffices.
